title: Beyond A∗: Better Planning with Transformers via Search Dynamics Bootstrapping
abstract: This paper introduces Searchformer, a Transformer model that solves complex planning tasks by imitating the search dynamics of the A∗ algorithm. Searchformer outperforms baselines and achieves state-of-the-art results on Sokoban puzzles, solving 93.7% of test tasks while using up to 26.8% fewer search steps than the A∗ implementation.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to find the shortest path in a maze. Traditional planners like A∗ are great at this, but they can be slow and inflexible. What if we could train a Transformer to solve these planning tasks by learning from A∗'s search dynamics?

This is the core insight behind Searchformer, a new approach that enables Transformers to solve complex planning tasks by imitating the search process of A∗.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
Searchformer works by training a Transformer to predict the search dynamics of A∗. This is done by expressing the planning task and its optimal solution plan as a sequence of words, or tokens. The Transformer is then trained to generate token sequences that encode A∗'s search dynamics along with an optimal plan.

The key innovation here is the use of search-augmented sequences, which include the execution trace of A∗ along with the optimal plan.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Searchformer achieves state-of-the-art results on Sokoban puzzles, solving 93.7% of test tasks while using up to 26.8% fewer search steps than the A∗ implementation. This is a significant improvement over baseline models, which solve only 90.3% of test tasks.

The results are even more impressive when considering the size of the model, with Searchformer outperforming larger baseline models.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
Searchformer has significant implications for planning and reasoning tasks. By learning to imitate the search dynamics of A∗, Searchformer can solve complex planning tasks more efficiently and effectively than traditional planners.

This has the potential to impact a wide range of applications, from robotics and autonomous vehicles to logistics and supply chain management.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The key innovation behind Searchformer is the use of search-augmented sequences, which include the execution trace of A∗ along with the optimal plan. This allows the Transformer to learn the search dynamics of A∗ and generate more efficient plans.

Another important innovation is the use of search dynamics bootstrapping, which enables the Transformer to improve its performance over time by generating new training data.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try Searchformer yourself, you can use the open-source implementation available on GitHub. This implementation includes pre-trained models and example code to get you started.

You can also experiment with different planning tasks and domains to see how Searchformer performs in different scenarios.
